messages.text: In a separate PR design and implement the endcap disk, with the same level of detail
I’ll design the short-strip endcap to match the tilted barrel, then implement and validate it in a separate PR with modules, support, mounting, cooling, cabling and service routes.

The old first-disc datum falls inside the barrel’s service collector. I’ll derive its replacement from the support thickness and the required 10 mm clearance, while retaining the old position as a coverage control.

For the local mechanics, I’m developing removable carbon-sandwich petals with embedded cooling and service exits at the outer edge. The model will reuse the barrel’s strixel stack and keep the fine coordinate tangential.

The Spack registry reports changed setup fingerprints. I’ll verify the DD4hep and Geant4 runtime directly before using it.

The proposed disc uses radial petals and the barrel’s strixel modules, with the fine measurement axis tangential. I’ll also check the combined barrel and endcap service load against the existing routing envelope.

The five-ring layout has 456 modules per disc on 12 removable petals. It keeps the barrel’s module stack and readout pitch, with smaller thermal pickups to fit the inner rings.

I’ve recorded the first-disc shift from 1295.5 to 1335 mm as an explicit design amendment. The other five datums remain fixed, and the coverage study will retain the old schedule as a control.

The first native check found support collisions: the initial ring counts put raised-module pickups through neighbouring lower modules. I’m revising the counts to leave clearance for the full module and its support, while retaining the failed candidate as evidence.

The coverage calculation agrees with the independent plane-intersection solver. It also shows losses near the annulus and first-disc transition; those will remain visible in the report.

The service ledger finds that combined barrel and endcap traffic exceeds the fixed downstream trunk’s nominal packing allowance by about 2.2%. I’ll keep that as an integration blocker.

The thermal screen also misses the sensor-temperature goal. I’m retaining those results alongside the geometry checks so a successful build cannot be mistaken for engineering qualification.

The revised 360-module disc passes native construction, material and identifier checks, with zero overlaps at the unchanged tolerance. A fresh ROOT process also reproduced all 4,320 sensor placements and signed axes.

The geometry needed two corrections beyond the ring counts: shorter pickups to clear adjacent flex ledges, and explicit rotation composition for the radial cooling lines. Both failed attempts remain recorded. I’m checking Geant4 transport and preparing the drawings for the PR.

Geant4 events exercised all six discs on each end, and the saved hits match the expected sensor IDs and primary-muon path lengths. The positive-side event also produced a secondary electron; the checker now uses saved particle relations to distinguish its hits.

I’ll publish this as a detailed prototype with the drawings and explicit coverage, thermal and service gates for review.

The final checks pass after adding the board mounts and increasing the local cooling entry bends to 10 mm. The engineering report still flags thermal resistance, support deflection, external turn space and combined trunk packing.

I’m publishing a separate draft PR stacked on the tilted-barrel PR. It will include the disc, petal and section drawings, reproducible checks, and recommendations for resolving those gates.

[PR #51](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/51) is open as a draft, stacked on #50. It includes the drawings in the description and links to the design, run instructions and validation report.

I’m finishing the publication log and checking the final hosted build.

I found a reporting error in the coverage summary: it claimed the old and new layouts had equal any-disc-hit counts, but had only recorded the new count. I’m measuring that comparison directly and correcting the report and PR description. The first-disc shift remains an explicit coverage gate.

The direct comparison confirms the first-disc shift removes the only short-strip endcap hit for 576 sampled tracks per charge sign at 4 T and pT = 1 GeV. That is 5.36% of tracks that hit the old endcap in each sample. I’m recording this as a coverage gate; the detailed geometry remains a draft prototype.

The geometry and transport checks passed, and the earlier hosted build succeeded. The revised coverage report now separates lost disc intersections from tracks losing their sole endcap hit. Thermal, support stiffness, cable bends and combined service packing also remain open gates for review.

PR #51 is open, stacked on the tilted-barrel PR #50. It contains the petal layout, support and service drawings, reproducible validation, and the corrected coverage result. I’m checking the hosted build for the correction commit before closing out.

The recommended starting point is twelve removable petals per disc, each carrying 30 modules and one cooling loop. Fine-pitch measurements stay tangential and coarse-pitch measurements radial. The three-seat mounting concept allows for thermal contraction; the stiffness screen indicates that an intermediate brace or a shell-and-joint analysis is still needed.

The local disc, boards and services fit inside the fixed radius bounds. Combined barrel/endcap service demand is still 2.2% above nominal trunk capacity. The design recommends resolving that with actual cable specifications and a shared service-entry design before integration.

The new endcap controls have passed in CI. The remaining hosted checks are dashboard and documentation validation. Both layout and cross-section drawings are in the PR description; the failed candidates and the coverage correction are retained in the evidence.

The session journal and project tracking validate. The final token counters for this implementation turn will only be available after it closes, so the record leaves them unknown and imports no partial counts.
The corrected endcap commit passed the full hosted build. I’m recording that result in the session closeout; this last update changes only logging metadata.

The closeout is pushed. It records the successful corrected build, preserves the original execution hashes, and validates in both checkouts. GitHub has started its usual checks for the two-file journal update; the scientific files match the commit that already passed.

The coverage study includes luminous-region offsets of −150, 0 and +150 mm, both charge signs, and 0/4 T field cases. It retains the original disc annuli and datums as controls, so the effect of moving the first disc stays visible in the comparison.

A final consistency check found a stale 456-module constant in the projected-area ratio; the layout itself has 360 modules per disc. I’m deriving the ratio from the placements and adding an independent area-accounting test. This changes the reported ratio, while the geometry and engineering gates remain unchanged.

The corrected area ratio is 1.355, and all nine portable controls pass. The full layout and native compact XML match the tested geometry byte for byte. Both earlier hosted builds succeeded; I’m publishing this last accounting correction and checking its build.

The negative endcap uses proper rotations and preserves the same tangential/radial measurement convention as the positive end. Native cell decoding, saved Geant4 crossings and ROOT persistence passed on both ends. The final source and artifact hashes also match the reproducibility inventory.

Each petal has a continuous titanium/CO₂ serpentine and separate power/data connections, supporting assembly and testing before installation. Tube forming, pressure drop and dry-out remain qualification work; the connected native geometry does not establish those properties.

All nine endcap controls have now passed in CI, including the sole-hit coverage and area-accounting regressions. The final run is completing the documentation and dashboard checks. No further geometry changes are planned for this PR.

The final build passed on `fd2ec9f`. PR #51 is ready for review as a draft prototype, with the corrected evidence included. Coverage at the first-disc transition, thermal performance, support stiffness and service routing remain explicit review gates.

Created [draft PR #51](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/51), stacked on the tilted-barrel PR #50.

It implements five rings with **360 modules per disc**, arranged on twelve removable petals, including support, mounting, titanium/CO₂ cooling, cabling and service routing. [DES-021]([redacted] records the reasoning and provenance.

DD4hep/ROOT, Geant4, nine portable controls and final CI passed; native overlaps are zero.

Review gates remain: the first-disc shift loses the sole endcap hit for **5.36% of old endcap-hit tracks** in each 1 GeV/4 T charge sample. Thermal, stiffness and service-routing screens also need revision.

Logging validates; this active turn’s final token counters remain unavailable.
